findings.message: Sanitize converted Markdown before inserting it into the DOM. When a user pastes Markdown containing raw HTML and switches to rich text, `marked.parse` preserves that HTML and this assignment inserts it into the application's live DOM. An image with an `onerror` handler can execute JavaScript in the authenticated application's origin. Server-side outgoing-mail sanitization happens too late to prevent this; sanitize the converted HTML before DOM insertion.

Export semantic HTML instead of Quill's internal markup. When composing bulleted or indented lists, Quill 2's editor DOM uses ordered-list elements with `data-list` attributes and Quill-specific classes to control their appearance. Sending `root.innerHTML` without Quill's stylesheet loses that formatting in recipients' mail clients, and Turndown also interprets bullet lists as numbered lists when switching modes. Export semantic HTML with Quill's `getSemanticHTML()` rather than its internal editor markup.

Validate the request before dereferencing recipient fields. For authenticated requests with `To` omitted or null, this dereference throws and returns a server error; null elements in any recipient array similarly fail at `email.Trim()`. The DTO's validation annotations are not automatically enforced because this application does not register Minimal API validation with `AddValidation()`, so subject/body limits and content-type constraints are also bypassed. Enable request validation and explicitly reject null recipient elements before processing the request.
